page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The instance features 24 physical cores with 24 vCPUs, utilizing a single thread per core configuration. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance operates on the KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and network-based resources.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.hfg6.6xlarge demonstrates stable mid-range performance. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1438.39 and a multi-core score of 23015.19, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 9875.0. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1282.13 GB/sec, which drops to 109.43 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. The instance delivers a static web serving throughput of 17.13 GB/sec and handles Redis SET operations at 22.14 million operations per second. For lightweight machine learning workloads, it processes 135M parameter LLM prompts at 1294.61 tokens per second, though performance drops to 34.44 tokens per second for 7B parameter models.

The absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU accelerators represents a clear tradeoff, making this instance unsuitable for high-IOPS database clustering or heavy deep learning training. However, the dedicated core allocation and 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth offer predictable performance for compute-intensive and general-purpose workloads. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a balanced resource density for enterprise applications. This profile is well-suited for multi-threaded application servers, web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations.
